newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: MARADONA HAS "SADDEST BIRTHDAY" DEFENDING MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: MARADONA HAS "SADDEST BIRTHDAY" DEFENDING MANAGER.

text.p: Argentina's fallen soccer idol Diego Maradona marked "the saddest birthday of his life" on Wednesday, promising never to abandon manager and friend Guillermo Coppola who is in jail on cocaine-dealing charges.
"People have told me 'forget Guillermo' but I won't ever forget my friend," the captain of the 1986 World Cup-winning side told reporters on his 36th birthday.

Maradona, who admits his own cocaine habit, gave evidence on Tuesday and corroborated Coppola's story that he knew nothing about the pound (400 grams) of cocaine that police found in a flower pot in his luxury Buenos Aires apartment.

The flashy 49-year-old playboy was charged with possession of drugs for sale and could face up to 20 years in jail. He says the drugs were planted at his home when he left it by one of three women who stayed there with Maradona after a party the weekend before the police raid.

"This is the saddest birthday of my life," Maradona said. "I want my friend out of jail. He's no saint but he's not as bad as they make him out. What is Guillermo? The most pathetic drug trafficker in the world?".
Maradona insisted there were "no drugs" at the party, just champagne and card games.
Once the world's top players, but now making only rare appearances for Boca Juniors, a grim-faced Maradona avoided the press on Tuesday but posed for pictures with court employees.
The case has degenerated into a soap opera, with members of the jet set and girlfriends half their age parading through television studios with lurid tales of drugs and prostitution.
Two women witnesses have admitted to "intimate relations" with the undercover policemen who bust Coppola while the judge and Coppola's lawyer engage in slanging-matches on television.
The case is embarrassing President Carlos Menem, who backs the death penalty for drug smugglers. Coppola was a friend of his late son Carlitos and private secretary Ramon Hernandez.

Maradona talks of "dark political and economic interests" behind Coppola's arrest and lashed out at local politicians on Wednesday. But many blame Coppola for Diego's drug habit which has earned him playing bans and recent charges of switched urine samples after a routine post-match drug test.
